Team —

We have EuroBank's cold-depot window confirmed for the week of Nov 16. This thread is to align the operational playbook for the offline artifact delivery, the signing ceremony, and the signer rotation cadence so the on-site operators and the courier have a single source of truth. Attaching an initial release manifest and a signing checklist for review.

Top-level asks:
- Confirm the list of authorized signers (Redwood + EuroBank) and the HSM/KMS handoff approach.
- Finalize the chain-of-custody form that the courier will carry and the operator will sign on receipt.
- Agree on acceptance tests (smoke + hash verification) and rollback trigger points.
- Confirm on-call matrix during the 48h post-install window.

Attachment highlights (attached): release-manifest-20261101.json — contains image hashes, manifest version, and staged artifacts; signing-ceremony-checklist.pdf — steps for detached signing + timestamping; chain_of_custody_form.xlsx — courier/operator signoff template.

Constraints / requirements from EuroBank (Claire): air-gapped site, no external NTP by default (we'll run an approved stratified time sync), and signed manifests must include RFC3161 timestamp. We should plan for an offline timestamping authority or use a TSP appliance that will be couriered for the ceremony.

Jonas — can you propose the signer rotation (who rotates keys, frequency, and the offline signer device ops) and the acceptance test script? Marissa — can you confirm operator runbook and the courier checklist with Henry? Mina / Priyom — thinking about emergency rollback: what's our smallest atomic rollback unit (image-level vs. node-level) and how do we preserve operator safety and auditability?

I'll coordinate with Claire on the exact drop-off window and share the courier ETA once Henry confirms routes.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Engineering Manager, Private Deployments

All —

Quick updates from runbook side after an internal dry run yesterday:
- Operator runbook (draft) covers pre-install hardware checks, manifest verification, hash verification (SHA-512), firewall isolation validation, and service startup smoke tests (health endpoint, KV cache warm).
- Courier checklist: sealed container verification, courier ID + company badge, two-person handover signoff, and tamper-evidence sticker placement. Henry, please confirm you can provide tamper-evidence seals of the same spec.
- Acceptance tests: node-level boot -> image sanity -> local inference smoke (5 queries, latency bounds) -> manifest re-hash -> sign-off.

I'll update the PDF checklist with explicit command snippets (sha512sum, detached signature verify steps using openssl cms -verify, and RFC3161 timestamp verification).

On rollback: propose we treat the image bundle as the atomic unit. If post-install smoke fails, we revert to the prior image bundle (stored on operator USB thumb for islanded recovery) and open an RCA. This minimizes the operator steps. Priyom / Mina — any objections?

Couple of technical notes and a proposed signer-rotation plan:

Signer rotation and signing mechanics:
- We will use detached CMS signatures for the images, produced by a hardware signing appliance (YubiHSM2-class) owned by Redwood. For EuroBank, authorized signers will countersign the manifest using their PIV-backed keys.
- Rotation cadence: appliance signing key (Redwood root) rotates yearly; operator signing keys (PIVs) rotate per customer request or every 6 months. For the rollout window, we will perform an ephemeral signer rotation: create a short-lived subordinate signing key, sign the release, and then escrow the subordinate key within the HSM and the audit log.
- Timestamping: generate RFC3161 timestamps from our staging TSP VM. If the site cannot reach a TSP, we will generate an RFC3161 receipt during the signing ceremony using a portable TSP appliance that will accompany the courier. The receipt is appended to the release manifest.

Acceptance/verification script (high level):
1) On operator console: verify sealed container serial and tamper seals.
2) Mount artifact media read-only; compute sha512sum and compare to manifest.
3) Verify detached signature: openssl cms -verify -in manifest.sig -content manifest.json -CAfile redwood-ca.pem
4) Verify RFC3161 receipt: rfc3161verify manifest.tsr against signed timestamp token.
5) Run smoke harness: smoke.sh --queries 5 --latency-threshold 200ms --report /tmp/smoke-report.json

Rollback and smallest atomic unit:
- Agree with Marissa: bundle-level rollback. We will keep the prior bundle encrypted on a second read-only media that the operator can swap to. Reversion requires an explicit on-call approval recorded in the chain_of_custody_form and an incident ticket created in our tracking system.

Observability notes: ensure we instrument the offline verification steps into the release-manifest as a checklist so the operator marks success/failure. This will be ingested into our audit pipeline when the site reconnects.

I'll push a small script repo (offline-verify v0.3) to the Drive link and include command examples.

-jw
